div.head: CHAP. V.

p.hi: 25. If we liue in the Spirit, let vs also walke in the Spirit.

div.p: In these words is cōtained, the last reason of the rule of good life before mentioned, in the 16. verse.

p.hi: 26. Let vs not be desirous of vaine-glorie, prouoking one another, enuying one another.

div.p: The scope. From this 26. verse, to the 11. verse of the chapter following. S. Paul handles the second Rule, which he had propounded in the 13. verse of this chapter: By loue serue one another.
THE SVPPLEMENT OR CONTINVATION OF the Commentarie vpon the sixt Chapter.
Printed by IOHN LEGAT, Printer to the Vniuersitie of CAMBRIDGE. 1604.

div.head: CHAP. VI.

p.hi: 1 Brethren, if a man be fallen by occasion into any fault, ye which are spirituall, restore such a one with the spirit of meekenes, considering thy selfe, least thou also be tempted.

div.p: TH' Apostle hauing finished the first part of the Instruction, touching the faith of the Galatians.

p.hi: 2. Beare ye one anothers burdens, and so fulfill the lawe of Christ.

div.p: In this verse, the Apostle propounds another rule, touching brotherly loue, and it dependeth vpon the former.

p.hi: 10. While we haue therefore time let vs doe good vnto all men, but specially to them which are of the houshold of faith.

div.p: In these words the Apostle doeth iterate the conclusion propounded in the sixt verse, as also in the ninth verse immediately going before.

p.hi: II Ye see how large a letter I haue written vnto you with mine owne hand.

div.p: Here beginneth the Conclusion, beeing the third generall part of this Epistle, consisting of two parts: an Insinuation, in the II. verse, & a Recapitulation, in the verses following.

p.hi: 12. As many as make a faire shew in the flesh, compell you to be circumcised, only because they would not suffer persecution for the crosse of Christ.

div.p: From hence to the ende, is laid down the second part of the conclusion, which I call a Recapitulation.

p.hi: 18. Brethren, the grace of our Lord Iesus Christ, be with your spirit, Amen.

div.p: Here, the Apostle concludes his epistle with his vsuall farewell commending the Galatians to the grace of God.

div.head: The Conclusion.
div.p: In the ende of all, it is added, in the Greeke, and Siriacke copies, that this Epistle was written to the Galatians from Rome. Which post-script seemes to be erroneous and false.
